title: Tools, training and limits
completeCaptionText:
Do not operate machinery just because its controls look simple. Training, permission and an appropriate supervised setting come first. Check hand tools before use: the handle must be secure, the working part sound and clean, and defects reported. Do not use a damaged tool.

Carry sharp tools so the blade or point is directed down and away from people, with enough space around you. Follow the trainer's demonstration for the particular tool; do not swing it, balance it across a shoulder near others or leave it in a walkway. Clean tools and appropriate clean gloves also help avoid contaminating the soil sample.

Before handling a fertilizer, pesticide, soil amendment or test reagent, read its label and the current Safety Data Sheet, or SDS. Older documents may say MSDS. Find its hazards, handling and storage instructions, protective measures and emergency information. Do not guess a chemical's hazards from its container colour or a test-result chart.
